findings.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:16 — Statistics updates join the User#save transaction, so rejecting a blocked email rolls back and discards match_count and last_match_at updates. Persist these statistics outside the failed user transaction.
app/models/blocked_email.rb:14 — The read-modify-save counter loses increments when concurrent checks read the same match_count and overwrite each other. Use an atomic database increment.

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:16 — Statistics updates join the User#save transaction, so rejecting a blocked email rolls back and discards match_count and last_match_at updates. Persist these statistics outside the failed user transaction.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue. Looking at the diff: BlockedEmail.should_block? is called from EmailValidator.validate_each (line 13 of email_validator.rb), which runs during User model validation. The should_block? method updates match_count and last_match_at with record.save (lines 14-16 of blocked_email.rb). When email validation fails, the User#save transaction will rollback, and since the BlockedEmail.save happens within the same request/validation context, these statistics updates would be lost if they're part of the same transaction. The finding correctly identifies that statistics tracking for blocked emails could be lost when the user creation fails.
